figures.caption: Figure 1: EEG decoding paradigms and relative performance. (a) Sliding-window classification and query-based event detection. (b) Performance of NeuroDETR and six baselines across eight datasets. Scores on each dataset are normalized by NeuroDETR’s score (NeuroDETR = 1).

Figure 2: Overview of NeuroDETR. (a) Continuous EEG input. (b) FOCAL uses event-presence estimates to guide local attention. (c) Temporal features are quantized at multiple resolutions. (d) Spatial-Pyramid VQ quantizes EEG features at global, regional, and local spatial levels. (e) A query decoder predicts event classes and boundaries from fused spatiotemporal memory. Detection and auxiliary losses provide training supervision.

Table 1: Results on eight EEG datasets: mean ± SD over five cross-validation folds, except TUSZ, which uses a single result on its predefined split. Best and second-best scores are bold and underlined, respectively.

Table 2: Core component ablations: F1event on eight EEG datasets (mean ± SD over five crossvalidation folds; TUSZ: a single result on its predefined split). Best and second-best scores are bold and underlined, respectively.

Figure 3: Temporal decoding examples from (a) BNCI2020 and (b) TUSZ. Colored intervals indicate event classes and temporal extents; GT denotes ground truth. Side panels report metrics computed on the displayed segments: eIoU is the mean temporal IoU over overlapping, same-class one-to-one matches, and event-level F1 (F1event) is evaluated at an IoU threshold of 0.5. N/A indicates that no matches are available for computing eIoU.
Figure 4: Event-level F1 of NeuroDETR and baseline methods at different temporal IoU thresholds. Higher thresholds impose stricter temporal localization requirements.

Figure 5: Event-level false negative rate (FNR) across eight datasets. Lower values indicate fewer missed events. NeuroDETR achieves the lowest FNR on six datasets. Error bars denote standard deviations and are omitted for TUSZ, where standard deviations are unavailable.

Figure 6: Event-level false discovery rate (FDR) across eight datasets. Lower values indicate a smaller proportion of incorrect detections among predictions. NeuroDETR achieves the lowest FDR on six datasets. Error bars denote standard deviations and are omitted for TUSZ, where standard deviations are unavailable.
Table 4: Sensitivity to decoder query count Ne. For each dataset, the upper and lower rows report Ne and F1event, respectively. Bold indicates the selected query count and its corresponding score.
Table 6: Dataset statistics and training configurations.
